summary: Short-lived session flood triggering autoscaler oscillation and transient GPU scarcity in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated transient throughput drops and P90 latency spikes on dedicated pool (Acme Health) over a 3-hour window. Symptoms coincide with a large number of extremely short sessions (connect -> request -> close) originating from a single tenant-driving connector, causing repeated GPU attach/detach churn and autoscaler oscillation. Impact: Customer experiencing intermittent 5-15% request failures (timeouts) and 40-110 ms P90 increase on batched routes during peak. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool 'dedicated-az1-acme', affected model pinned to open-7b-v2. Steps to reproduce (observed): 1) At ~09:12 UTC a burst of ~18k short sessions over 10 minutes started from tenant connector cluster. 2) Autoscaler reacted by scaling up 6 GPU slots; as sessions ended rapidly autoscaler scaled down aggressively, causing rebalancing and multiple preemptive evictions. 3) Repeated attach/detach sequences created transient GPU scarcity: new attach requests saw >500ms attach latency, some timed out and triggered fallback routing. 4) Symptoms improved once short-session flood subsided; ~30 minutes of tail effects remained. Logs/metrics: support attached time series (internal): attach_latency.p95 spiked to 620ms, allocator.failed_attach increased by 3.2x, autoscaler.scale_events increased to 27 in 15m, batch_queue_depth oscillated. Temporary workaround: Suggested customer throttle client-side connector concurrency and increase session keepalive to amortize attach cost. Support recommended enabling short-session smoothing policy (experimental) while we investigate.

investigation_notes: Initial correlational analysis: high short-session rate from tenant connector cluster 10.0.55.0/22 between 09:12-09:22 UTC coincides with autoscaler event storm.
Allocator traces show multiple attach requests queued waiting for NVLink initialization leading to ~3-4 concurrent attach spikes per GPU node.
Autoscaler configured with aggressive downscale cooldown (30s) in this pool; too reactive for ephemeral traffic patterns. Scale-downs caused eviction waves and subsequent scale-ups in <2m windows.
Batcher metrics show fragmentation: many small streams prevented efficient batching and left GPU slots underutilized while still counted toward capacity, worsening perceived scarcity.
Customer connector behavior (one TCP connect per request) significantly increases attach/detach frequency. Recommending best practices to keep sessions alive or multiplex requests.
No evidence of hardware faults or driver crashes; root cause is workload pattern interacting poorly with autoscaler heuristics and slot accounting.
Smoothing policy (session aggregation + longer down-cooldown) replicates improvement in staging: fewer scale cycles, lower attach latency, and increased end-to-end success rate.
Risk assessment: defaulting cooldown changes globally could increase cost for genuinely idle pools; plan to rollout opt-in smoothing with telemetry and guardrails.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer throttled connector and increased keepalive -> immediate reduction in errors. Support applied targeted autoscaler down-cooldown increase (30s->180s) and enabled session-aggregation sidecar for the affected dedicated pool.
Engineers prepared PR #842 to introduce an autoscaler smoothing policy (opt-in) that combines session-duration heuristics, minimum up-time guarantees for new GPUs, and batcher-aware slot accounting.

Canary rollout plan: test smoothing policy on 5% of dedicated pools for 48h, monitor attach_latency.p95, scale_events rate, and billing delta metrics. If stable, expand to dedicated pools with similar noisy-tenant patterns.

Follow-ups: 1) Postmortem documenting root cause and customer guidance (owners: Marcus, Elena) due 2026-03-20. 2) Customer docs detailing connector best practices and recommended server-side config. 3) Telemetry alert to detect short-session flood patterns and recommend automatic soft-throttle advisory to tenants.
Status: Mitigation in place; customer stable. Engineering work in progress for long-term guardrail.
